output.answer_markdown: NRG identifies several risks in acquiring businesses, assets, or customer books. Acquisitions are subject to substantial risks, including failing to identify material problems in due diligence, over-paying for assets or customers, losing customers, and being unable to arrange needed financing [1]. Integration requires substantial resources, and acquisitions may ultimately not be successfully integrated [2]. For dispositions, risks may relate to employment matters, counterparties, regulators and other stakeholders, separating the disposed assets, and other financial, legal and operational risks [3]. NRG may also be subject to material trailing liabilities from disposed businesses [4]. Any such risk may result in costly disputes or litigation [5]. If the anticipated returns or benefits from an acquisition or disposition are not realized, NRG's results of operations, cash flows and financial condition could be adversely affected [6]. For the Direct Energy acquisition specifically, failure to achieve anticipated benefits could mean increased costs, lower-than-expected revenues or income, and diversion of management's time and energy [7].
